note: Every increment races with every other thread, which is exactly the case atomicAdd exists to make safe.
A __host__ __device__ function compiles twice, once for the CPU path and once for the GPU path.
Every CUDA call returns a status; wrapping it in a macro is the only way anyone actually checks it.
cudaEventElapsedTime needs both events recorded and synchronized first, or the reading is undefined.
A grid-stride loop lets one launch config handle any n, since each thread just wraps around the whole grid.
A 2D launch still flattens to one linear offset; row-major means width multiplies the row index.
The <<<grid, block>>> syntax is CUDA's own extension; nvcc strips it before handing off to the host compiler.
cudaMemcpyHostToDevice and cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost are opposite directions; mixing them up corrupts silently.
Sequential addressing halves the active-thread stride each round, which avoids the shared-memory bank conflicts of the naive version.
__shfl_down_sync exchanges registers directly between lanes, so the final warp needs no shared memory at all.
__syncthreads() must be reached by every thread in the block, so it cannot sit inside a divergent branch.
A stream orders its own operations but runs independently of other streams, which is how copy overlaps compute.
Tiling loads each element from global memory once per tile instead of once per output, which is the whole win.
Padding each row by one element shifts the column stride so it no longer aliases the same bank.
cudaMallocManaged gives one pointer valid on both sides; prefetch hides the migration latency ahead of use.
